Container.Name: Filtarr
Container.Overview: Filtarr keeps your Sonarr and Radarr libraries organized with simple, ordered rules. Send kids' titles to a Kids library, move shows nobody has watched in 90 days, tag movies that are streaming on Netflix, and more, using over 100 details from Sonarr, Radarr, Plex watch history, Tautulli, TMDB and OMDb. Preview every change before it runs, schedule runs, and see a full history of what moved and who did it. Sign in with Plex; the first account becomes the owner.[br][br]First start: open the container log and copy the one-time setup token, then open the WebUI and sign in with Plex.
Container.Requires: Sonarr and/or Radarr. Plex is used for sign-in.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the Filtarr web interface and API. Uses Host networking by default, like Overseerr, so Sonarr, Radarr, Tautulli and Plex can be reached at localhost or the server's LAN address.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Database and encryption key. Back up both files together: the key decrypts your saved API keys.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: Optional. Only needed behind a reverse proxy: the public https:// address, e.g. https://filtarr.example.com. Leave empty for LAN use.

Config.Name: Trust reverse proxy
Config.Description: Set to true only when Filtarr is reached through a reverse proxy, so it sees real client addresses. Leave false when clients connect directly.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID that owns the config folder.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID that owns the config folder.

Config.Name: Secret key
Config.Description: Optional. 64 hex characters. Leave empty and Filtarr creates filtarr.db.key in the config folder on first start.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: How much the container log shows.
